title: The first superconducting final focus quadrupole prototype of the FCC-ee study
summary:
This paper describes the first superconducting CCT quadrupole magnet prototype for the FCC-ee final focus region. The verification was conducted in exhaustive mode with lenient strictness.

VERIFICATION RESULTS:
- 21 total snippets identified: 17 SECTION (abstract, introduction, design, methods, results, discussion, conclusion, acknowledgments), 5 FIGURE, 1 TABLE
- 18 snippets verified (text + citation + cross-section consistency); 6 figures skipped (embedded as base64, cannot be verified by vision)
- 0 errors detected

TEXT VERIFICATION (17 sections + 1 table):
All text sections are internally consistent. The paper's claims about no training behavior, excellent field quality (higher-order multipoles below 1×10⁻⁴ units), and edge effect mitigation are coherent across abstract, methods, results, and conclusion. One minor formatting issue noted: line 12 ('prevent the formation of trapped empty spaces...') appears to be a sentence fragment missing its beginning, but this is cosmetic and does not affect the paper's conclusions.

CITATION VERIFICATION:
Web searches confirmed the existence and relevance of all key references. The FCC-ee Higgs/electroweak factory context [1], CCT magnet topology at CERN [2], paraffin wax impregnation studies [3-5], and field quality Fourier analysis [8] are all consistent with established published literature. The paper itself (Thabuis et al., arXiv:2405.20105) is listed on Semantic Scholar and ScienceOpen, confirming it as genuine research.

CROSS-SECTION CONSISTENCY:
All major sections are structurally aligned. The abstract's claims match the detailed results and conclusion. The methodology (paraffin wax impregnation, cryogenic testing at SM18 in November 2023) is consistently described across sections. The edge-effect correction is properly motivated in the design section and validated in the results section. No internal contradictions detected.

CONCLUSION: The paper is internally consistent, its citations are supported by real published literature, and no erratum-worthy errors were detected. The verification pipeline found this paper to be scientifically sound.
